newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: CMG aims to outperform market.
newsitem.headline: CMG aims to outperform market.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch computer services firm CMG Plc said on Monday it would again aim to outperform its markets in 1997.
"In the Netherlands, we aim to continue growing faster than the market and to maintain our margins in the 14 to 16 percent range," chairman Cor Stutterheim said in a statement.
"In the UK, we are aiming for continued growth in turnover and profit," he added.
CMG said it would make considerable investments in banking and insurance software products. It has restructured its German operations and said it expected improved results there.

"The overall effect will be for the group to show further good profitable growth in 1997, even though we publish our accounts in sterling, which is currently much stronger than in 1996," the company said.
CMG earlier reported 1996 net profit from ordinary operations of 17.1 million stg, up 37 percent from 1995's 12.5 million stg.

It said demand for its IT services and products rose in Britain and the Netherlands in particular. Dutch turnover surged by 35 percent to 172 million stg and operating profit went up by 38 percent to 27.1 million stg in this area.
Overall turnover in Britain increased by nine percent, reflecting CMG's withdrawal from the share registration market at the start of 1996.
"Excluding this, underlying growth (in Britain) was a healthy 20 percent while operating profit improved by 69 percent," CMG said.

The German unit ended 1996 with a significant but unspecified loss, which included one-off costs of redundancies and reorganisations. CMG said solving the problems at its German unit had taken longer than expected but added the difficulties had now been addressed.
"The vast majority of our German operations performed reasonably well and we now expect a much improved performance there in 1997," CMG said.
The acquisition of Germany's Orga Team by the end of 1996 had strengthened its position there and was expected to contribute to this year's group earnings.

CMG said sustainable organic growth would be its first priority but said it would also continue to look for good acquisitions which would add value in terms of product, market or geographical presence.
